#KOMPAS #BritishWatchmakers #BritishWatchAndClockMakers #IndependentWatchmaking #microbrandwatch

Kompas Watches have made their debut with a quartet of RAF inspired field watches that make use of the iconic Dowding System sector clock, a stylised clock display used in RAF operations rooms designed to easily differentiate between recent and outdated reports from radar teams and reconnaissance data. Kompas recreate its distinctive triangular markings in either green, blue, grey or red, with each dedicated to a cardinal point of the compass, hence the brand name.

⏰ EAST

Today, I would like to introduce you to a new brand from London, UK. These guys are bringing a piece of military history straight to the wrist with their first watch inspired by the RAF Sector Clock, invented in 1917! You can find a lot of info online about that genius invention which saved countless lives during WWII but today I want to talk about this beautiful field watch. 
What can go wrong with this gorgeously proportioned 316L sandblasted stainless steel piece that features a gorgeous performance layer compass dial resembling RAF Sector Clock, sapphire crystal, and super reliable Japanese automatic movement? In my opinion, absolutely nothing as it presents a pretty much perfect field watch, and on top of that, it is designed with beautiful details! 
Amazing first release and such a cool backstory for watch design! 👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻

❓What do you think about this release? Let me know👇🏻

G.L.C. × KOMPAS

We are thrilled to announce our collaboration with G.L.C. Straps.

At the heart of this project is an original Falklands era military coat, a remarkable piece of British military heritage that carries decades of history, character and craftsmanship. Through this collaboration, that legacy will continue its journey, transformed into a limited collection of handmade watch straps.

This is a project built on a shared appreciation for authentic materials, purposeful design and the stories that endure through time.

We cannot wait to share the final result with you.

RAF sector clock: the clock that guarded the skies, and the dial it gave KOMPAS.

1917: the Royal Flying Corps tracks raids on London by colour, not by the minute.
1936: the sector clock joins the Dowding System. Detect, filter, plot.
1939–1945: WAAF plotters match every raid marker to the red, yellow and blue triangles on the wall.
Today: twelve layered triangles, five minutes each, on your wrist.

Full story: kompaswatches.com/history

From command rooms to open skies.

Developed for RAF operations, the Sector Clock divided each hour into colour coded five minute segments, allowing controllers to read the freshness of incoming reports instantly. Instead of calculating time stamps, they saw them. Red, blue, yellow markers translated radar and observer data into immediate tactical decisions.

Time became visual. Information became actionable. Direction became decisive.

Discover the full story in our History section at kompaswatches.com

#RAFSectorClock #AviationHistory #OperationalDesign #BritishEngineering #FindYourDirection

The KOMPAS Performance Layer translates the operational timing logic of the RAF Sector Clock into a modern wrist instrument. Each triangular marker represents a precise 5 minute sector, creating a colour coded interval system that allows rapid temporal positioning at a glance.

The multi layer dial architecture separates timing structure from base dial, improving legibility, depth, and spatial clarity.

This is not decoration.
It is a functional timing interface.
